Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 24, verse 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that they both said: "Surat al-Nur was revealed at Madinah."

Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab reported from ʿAʾishah, as a marfuʿ report: "Do not let them (women) live in upper rooms, and do not teach them writing; but teach them spinning and Surat al-Nur." (The phrase "i.e., the women" is in the text.)

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi reported from Mujahid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Teach your men Surat al-Ma'idah, and teach your women Surat al-Nur." This is a mursal report.

Abu ʿUbayd in his Fada'il reported from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab wrote to us: "Learn Surat al-Nisa', al-Ahzab and al-Nur."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory, and in which We have sent down clear verses, that you may remember.﴾ ﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator: flog each one of them a hundred lashes. And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater; and that has been forbidden to the believers.﴾

(p-996) Al-surah linguistically means a noble rank, and for this reason a portion of the Qur'an is called a surah. From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"Did you not see that Allah has given you a surah (rank), so that every king below it wavers?"

That is, a rank. The majority read surah with a nominative ending (surah-un), and there are two possibilities in this: first, that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "this is a surah"; al-Zajjaj, al-Farra' and al-Mubarrad preferred this, saying: because it is indefinite, and one does not begin with an indefinite noun in every position.

The second possibility is that it is the subject, and beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is qualified by His words "which We have sent down" (anzalnaha), and the predicate is "the fornicatress and the fornicator." The meaning would be: "the surah which is sent down and made obligatory is such-and-such," since a surah is an expression for a sequence of verses having a beginning and an end. This is a sound meaning, and there is no basis for what the earlier scholars said, that beginning with it is prohibited because it is indefinite; it is an indefinite noun specified by a qualifier, and beginning with it is agreed upon as permissible.

It has been said: it is a subject whose predicate is omitted, with the sense: "among what has been revealed to you is a surah." This was rejected, because the context calls for explaining the status of this noble surah, not for stating that among what was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) there is a surah of such-and-such a status.

Al-Hasan ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, ʿIsa al-Thaqafi, ʿIsa al-Kufi, Mujahid, Abu Haywah and Talhah ibn Musarrif read it in the accusative (surata). There are several possibilities in this: the first is that it is accusative by a verb omitted and not explained by what follows, its estimate being "recite a surah" or "read a surah."

The second is that it is accusative by a hidden verb which is explained by what follows, according to what is said regarding the construction where the verb is occupied with its pronoun: i.e., "We sent down a surah, We have sent it down." Thus "anzalnaha" here has no place in grammatical analysis, because it is an explanatory clause; unlike the previous possibility, where it is in the accusative position as a qualifier of "surah."

The third possibility is that it is accusative as an exhortation, i.e., "take a surah" (duka surah). This was said by the author of al-Kashshaf. Abu Hayyan rejected it, saying that it is not permissible to omit the particle of exhortation.

The fourth is that it is accusative as a circumstantial (hal) from the pronoun of "anzalnaha." Al-Farra' said: it is a circumstantial from the ha' and alif, and a circumstantial from a pronoun may precede it. On this view the pronoun in "anzalnaha" does not refer to "surah" but to the rulings, as if it were said: "We sent down the rulings in the state of being a surah from the surahs of the Qur'an."

Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read "wa-farradnaha" with shaddah (intensive), and the rest read it without shaddah.

Abu ʿAmr said: "farradnaha" with shaddah means: We divided it in its sending down, portion by portion; and al-fard means cutting. It may also be that the shaddah indicates multiplicity or emphasis. The meaning of the lightened form is: We made it obligatory and made it something decided upon. It has also been said: We obligated you to act upon it; and it has been said: We determined the prescribed limits within it. Al-fard means determination, and from it is "Indeed He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an" (28:85). "And We sent down in it clear verses": that is, We sent down within its folds and contents. The meaning of their being clear is that their indication of what they signify is evident. The repetition of "anzalna" is for complete care in sending down this surah, because of the rulings it contains.

﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator﴾: this begins the detailed explanation of what was stated in summary among the clear verses. It is in the nominative as a subject, and the predicate is "flog each one of them"; or it is in the predicative sense for "surah," as has preceded. Zina is the intercourse of a man with a woman in her private part without marriage or the semblance of marriage.

It has also been said: it is the insertion of a private part into a private part which is naturally desired and legally forbidden. The fornicatress is the woman who submits to fornication and enables it, as the form indicates, not the one who is coerced; likewise the fornicator. The entry of the fa' into the predicate is because the subject implies the sense of a condition, according to the view of al-Akhfash. As for the view of Sibawayh, the predicate is omitted, and the estimate is: "In what is recited to you, the ruling on the fornicatress..." Then He explained that with His words: "flog."

Al-jald means striking; one says: "jaladahu" when he struck his skin, like "batanahu" when he struck his belly, and "ra'asahu" when he struck his head. His words "a hundred lashes" are the punishment for the free, adult, unmarried fornicator, and likewise the fornicatress. The Sunnah established an addition to this lashing, which is banishment for a year. As for the slave, male and female, each receives fifty lashes, based on His words: "If they commit a gross indecency, then upon them is half the punishment for free chaste women" (4:25). This is explicit regarding female slaves, and male slaves are added to them for lack of a distinguishing factor. As for the one who is muhsan (married), the penalty is stoning, by the authentic, widely transmitted Sunnah and by the consensus of the people of knowledge; indeed, and by the Qur'an whose wording was abrogated while its ruling remains, which is: "The elderly man and the elderly woman, if they commit fornication, stone them absolutely." A group of the people of knowledge added a hundred lashes along with stoning. We have clarified what is correct in this matter in our commentary on al-Muntaqa. The discussion of the penalty for zina has already passed in full. This verse abrogates the verse of confinement and the verse of harm, which are in Surat al-Nisa'.

ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Thaqafi, Yahya ibn Yaʿmur, Abu Ja'far and Abu Shaybah read "al-zaniyata wa-l-zaniya" with the accusative. It has been said this is the analogical form according to Sibawayh, since in his view it is like your saying "Zaydan, strike."

As for al-Farra', al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj, the nominative is preferable in their view, and the majority read it so.

The reason for placing the fornicatress before the fornicator here is that fornication in that time was more common among women, to the extent that they had banners set up at their doors so that whoever intended the indecency could recognize them.

It has also been said: the reason for the precedence is that the woman is the origin of the act; it has been said: because desire is stronger in her and she is more prone to it; and it has been said: because the shame attached to women is greater, since their station is that of veiling and protection. So He mentioned the fornicatress first, as an intensification and a matter of concern.

The address in this verse is to the rulers and those who stand in their place. It has also been said: it is addressed to all Muslims, because establishing the hudud is obligatory upon them all, and the imam acts on their behalf, since it is not possible for them all to gather to establish the hudud. ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾: it is said raʾufa yarʾufu raʾfatan on the pattern of faʿlah, and raʾafatan on the pattern of faʿalah, like al-nashʾah and al-nashaʾah; both mean tenderness and mercy. It has been said: it is the subtlest of mercy.

The majority read "raʾfatun" with the hamzah sukun, Ibn Kathir read it with fatha, and Ibn Jurayj read "raʾafatun" with the madd, on the pattern of faʿalah. The meaning of "in the religion of Allah" is in His obedience and His judgment, as in His words: "He could not take his brother under the king's law" (12:76). Then He said, confirming for those commanded and stirring them: "if you believe in Allah and the Last Day," as you say to a man urging him to a matter: "If you are a man, then do such-and-such." That is: if you affirm the Oneness of God and the Resurrection in which the recompense of deeds lies, then do not suspend the hudud. ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾: that is, let them be present to add to the deterrence against them both, and to the spreading of shame upon them and the publicizing of their disgrace. A ṭāʾifah is the group that surrounds a thing, from al-tawf; the least number of a ṭāʾifah is three, and it has been said two, and it has been said one, and it has been said four, and it has been said ten.

Then He, glorified, mentioned something specific to the fornicator and the fornicatress, saying: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. The people of knowledge have differed on the meaning of this verse, in several views:

The first: that its intent is to censure fornication and censure its practitioners, and that it is forbidden to the believers; "the fornicator marries" means intercourse, not contract; that is, the fornicator does not commit fornication except with a fornicatress, and the fornicatress does not commit it except with a fornicator. He added mention of the idolatress and the idolater because polytheism is more general among sins than fornication. Al-Zajjaj rejected this and said: marriage in the Book of Allah is known only in the sense of wedlock. This rejection is answered by the fact that nikah in the sense of intercourse is established in the Book of Allah, glorified be He, and from it is His words: "until she marries another husband" (2:230); the Prophet (ﷺ) explained that the intended meaning there is intercourse. Among those who said that the meaning of "the fornicator marries none but a fornicatress" is "the fornicator does not commit fornication except with a fornicatress" are Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿIkrimah, as Ibn Jarir related from them, and al-Khattabi related it from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second view: this verse was revealed concerning a specific woman, as will be explained, so it is specific to her, as al-Khattabi said.

The third view: it was revealed concerning a certain man among the Muslims, so it is specific to him, as Mujahid said.

The fourth: it was revealed concerning the people of the Suffah, so it is specific to them, as Abu Salih said.

The fifth: that the intent of "the fornicator and the fornicatress" is those who have received the hadd punishment; this was related by al-Zajjaj and others from al-Hasan, who said: "This is a ruling from Allah, so it is not permissible for a fornicator who has received the hadd to marry anyone but one who has received the hadd." Something similar was narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and some of al-Shafi'i's companions held this view. Ibn al-ʿArabi said: this meaning is not sound by reasoning, just as it is not established by transmission.

The sixth: that this verse is abrogated by His words, glorified be He: "And marry the single among you" (24:32). Al-Nahhas said: most scholars hold this view.

The seventh view: that this ruling is founded upon the majority. The meaning is: the majority of fornicators desire to marry none but a fornicatress like themselves, and the majority of fornicatresses should desire to marry none but a fornicator like them; and the intent is to deter believers from marrying fornicatresses after deterring them from fornication. This is the most preponderant of the views, and the occasion of revelation supports it, as will come.

It has been differed regarding the permissibility of a man marrying a woman with whom he himself committed fornication. Al-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifah held that this is permissible.

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, and narrated from ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿud and Jabir, that it is not permissible.

Ibn Masʿud said: If a man commits fornication with a woman and then marries her afterward, they are both fornicators forever; and Malik held this view. The meaning of "and that has been forbidden to the believers" is the marriage of fornicatresses, because of what it contains of resemblance to the wicked, exposure to suspicion, and reproach regarding lineage.

It has been said: it is merely disliked, and "forbidden" is used to mean the disliked-for-purity sense (karahat al-tanzih), for the sake of emphasis in deterrence.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words "A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory": he said: "We have made it clear."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported through the chain of ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar: that a slave girl of Ibn ʿUmar committed fornication, and he struck her legs and back. I said: "And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah." He said: "O my son, did you see that pity took hold of me? Indeed Allah did not command me to kill her or to flog her head; and I have indeed inflicted pain where I struck."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 24, verse 1–3 (part 2 of 2):

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ that he said: "The group (ṭāʾifah) is a man or more."

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh (al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh, on abrogation), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, and al-Diya al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtarah narrated through the route of Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿The adulterer does not marry﴾ that he said: "This is not about marriage (nikah) but about intercourse (jima'). No one commits adultery with her when he commits adultery except an adulterer or a polytheist." ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾ meaning adultery.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾ that he said: "The women in the Jahiliyyah were prostitutes (baghiyyat), and among them was a beautiful woman called Umm Jamil. A man from among the Muslims would marry one of them so that she would spend on him from her earnings. So Allah, glory be to Him, forbade any of the Muslims from marrying them." This is a mursal report.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Sulayman ibn Yasar something similar, in brief.

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from ʿAtaʾ from Ibn Abbas, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah there were prostitutes, the prostitutes of such-and-such a family and the prostitutes of such-and-such a family. So Allah said: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾, the verse... and Allah settled that matter concerning the affair of the Jahiliyyah." Something similar to this is reported from a group of the Tabiʿun.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated from al-Dahhak regarding the verse that he said: "It only refers to adultery and does not refer to marriage."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr something similar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from ʿIkrimah something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse that he said: "The adulterer from among the People of the Qiblah does not commit adultery except with a female adulterer like himself from among the People of the Qiblah, or a polytheist woman from outside the People of the Qiblah. And the female adulterer from among the People of the Qiblah does not commit adultery except with a male adulterer like herself from among the People of the Qiblah, or a polytheist man from outside the People of the Qiblah. And adultery is forbidden to the believers."

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: "There was a woman called Umm Mahzul, who used to fornicate and would stipulate that he spend on her. A man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to marry her, so Allah revealed: ﴿The adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist﴾."

Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "There was a man called Marthad, who used to carry captives from Makkah until he brought them to Madinah. In Makkah there was a prostitute called ʿAnaq, who was a friend of his." He mentioned a story in which: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I marry ʿAnaq?' He did not answer me at all until the verse was revealed: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾, the verse. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Marthad, ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾, so do not marry her.'"

Ibn Jarir narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr regarding the verse that he said: "They were known women. A man from among the poor Muslims would marry one of them so that she would spend on him, and Allah forbade them from that."

Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning open prostitutes who were in the Jahiliyyah, who were adulteresses and polytheists, so Allah forbade marrying them to the believers.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Shu'bah, the mawla of Ibn Abbas, who said: "I was with Ibn Abbas when a man came to him and said: 'I used to pursue a woman and I had from her what Allah had forbidden me. Allah has granted me repentance from her, and I wish to marry her.' The people said: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾. Ibn Abbas said: 'This is not the place of this verse. They were prostitutes who openly displayed themselves, who would place banners at their doors, by which people would recognize them. So Allah revealed this verse. Marry her, and if there is any sin in it, it is upon me.'"

Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn ʿAdi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The adulterer who has been flogged does not marry except one like himself."

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that a man married a woman, then he committed adultery and the prescribed punishment was carried out on him. They brought him to ʿAli, and he separated him from his wife and said: "Do not marry except a flogged woman like yourself."

ʿIsa ibn ʿUmar al-Thaqafi, Yahya ibn Yaʿmur, Abu Ja'far and Abu Shaybah read "al-zaniyata wa-l-zaniya" with the accusative. It has been said this is the analogical form according to Sibawayh, since in his view it is like your saying "Zaydan, strike."

As for al-Farra', al-Mubarrad and al-Zajjaj, the nominative is preferable in their view, and the majority read it so.

The reason for placing the fornicatress before the fornicator here is that fornication in that time was more common among women, to the extent that they had banners set up at their doors so that whoever intended the indecency could recognize them.

It has also been said: the reason for the precedence is that the woman is the origin of the act; it has been said: because desire is stronger in her and she is more prone to it; and it has been said: because the shame attached to women is greater, since their station is that of veiling and protection. So He mentioned the fornicatress first, as an intensification and a matter of concern.

The address in this verse is to the rulers and those who stand in their place. It has also been said: it is addressed to all Muslims, because establishing the hudud is obligatory upon them all, and the imam acts on their behalf, since it is not possible for them all to gather to establish the hudud. ﴿And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah﴾: it is said raʾufa yarʾufu raʾfatan on the pattern of faʿlah, and raʾafatan on the pattern of faʿalah, like al-nashʾah and al-nashaʾah; both mean tenderness and mercy. It has been said: it is the subtlest of mercy.

The majority read "raʾfatun" with the hamzah sukun, Ibn Kathir read it with fatha, and Ibn Jurayj read "raʾafatun" with the madd, on the pattern of faʿalah. The meaning of "in the religion of Allah" is in His obedience and His judgment, as in His words: "He could not take his brother under the king's law" (12:76). Then He said, confirming for those commanded and stirring them: "if you believe in Allah and the Last Day," as you say to a man urging him to a matter: "If you are a man, then do such-and-such." That is: if you affirm the Oneness of God and the Resurrection in which the recompense of deeds lies, then do not suspend the hudud. ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾: that is, let them be present to add to the deterrence against them both, and to the spreading of shame upon them and the publicizing of their disgrace. A ṭāʾifah is the group that surrounds a thing, from al-tawf; the least number of a ṭāʾifah is three, and it has been said two, and it has been said one, and it has been said four, and it has been said ten.

Then He, glorified, mentioned something specific to the fornicator and the fornicatress, saying: ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress﴾. The people of knowledge have differed on the meaning of this verse, in several views:

The first: that its intent is to censure fornication and censure its practitioners, and that it is forbidden to the believers; "the fornicator marries" means intercourse, not contract; that is, the fornicator does not commit fornication except with a fornicatress, and the fornicatress does not commit it except with a fornicator. He added mention of the idolatress and the idolater because polytheism is more general among sins than fornication. Al-Zajjaj rejected this and said: marriage in the Book of Allah is known only in the sense of wedlock. This rejection is answered by the fact that nikah in the sense of intercourse is established in the Book of Allah, glorified be He, and from it is His words: "until she marries another husband" (2:230); the Prophet (ﷺ) explained that the intended meaning there is intercourse. Among those who said that the meaning of "the fornicator marries none but a fornicatress" is "the fornicator does not commit fornication except with a fornicatress" are Saʿid ibn Jubayr, Ibn ʿAbbas and ʿIkrimah, as Ibn Jarir related from them, and al-Khattabi related it from Ibn ʿAbbas.

The second view: this verse was revealed concerning a specific woman, as will be explained, so it is specific to her, as al-Khattabi said.

The third view: it was revealed concerning a certain man among the Muslims, so it is specific to him, as Mujahid said.

The fourth: it was revealed concerning the people of the Suffah, so it is specific to them, as Abu Salih said.

The fifth: that the intent of "the fornicator and the fornicatress" is those who have received the hadd punishment; this was related by al-Zajjaj and others from al-Hasan, who said: "This is a ruling from Allah, so it is not permissible for a fornicator who has received the hadd to marry anyone but one who has received the hadd." Something similar was narrated from Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, and some of al-Shafi'i's companions held this view. Ibn al-ʿArabi said: this meaning is not sound by reasoning, just as it is not established by transmission.

The sixth: that this verse is abrogated by His words, glorified be He: "And marry the single among you" (24:32). Al-Nahhas said: most scholars hold this view.

The seventh view: that this ruling is founded upon the majority. The meaning is: the majority of fornicators desire to marry none but a fornicatress like themselves, and the majority of fornicatresses should desire to marry none but a fornicator like them; and the intent is to deter believers from marrying fornicatresses after deterring them from fornication. This is the most preponderant of the views, and the occasion of revelation supports it, as will come.

It has been differed regarding the permissibility of a man marrying a woman with whom he himself committed fornication. Al-Shafi'i and Abu Hanifah held that this is permissible.

It is narrated from Ibn ʿAbbas, and narrated from ʿUmar, Ibn Masʿud and Jabir, that it is not permissible.

Ibn Masʿud said: If a man commits fornication with a woman and then marries her afterward, they are both fornicators forever; and Malik held this view. The meaning of "and that has been forbidden to the believers" is the marriage of fornicatresses, because of what it contains of resemblance to the wicked, exposure to suspicion, and reproach regarding lineage.

It has been said: it is merely disliked, and "forbidden" is used to mean the disliked-for-purity sense (karahat al-tanzih), for the sake of emphasis in deterrence.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Ibn ʿAbbas concerning His words "A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory": he said: "We have made it clear."

ʿAbd al-Razzaq, ʿAbd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim reported through the chain of ʿUbayd Allah ibn ʿAbd Allah ibn ʿUmar: that a slave girl of Ibn ʿUmar committed fornication, and he struck her legs and back. I said: "And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah." He said: "O my son, did you see that pity took hold of me? Indeed Allah did not command me to kill her or to flog her head; and I have indeed inflicted pain where I struck."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 24, verse 1–3 (part 2 of 2):

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ that he said: "The group (ṭāʾifah) is a man or more."

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh (al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh, on abrogation), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, and al-Diya al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtarah narrated through the route of Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿The adulterer does not marry﴾ that he said: "This is not about marriage (nikah) but about intercourse (jima'). No one commits adultery with her when he commits adultery except an adulterer or a polytheist." ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾ meaning adultery.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾ that he said: "The women in the Jahiliyyah were prostitutes (baghiyyat), and among them was a beautiful woman called Umm Jamil. A man from among the Muslims would marry one of them so that she would spend on him from her earnings. So Allah, glory be to Him, forbade any of the Muslims from marrying them." This is a mursal report.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Sulayman ibn Yasar something similar, in brief.

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from ʿAtaʾ from Ibn Abbas, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah there were prostitutes, the prostitutes of such-and-such a family and the prostitutes of such-and-such a family. So Allah said: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾, the verse... and Allah settled that matter concerning the affair of the Jahiliyyah." Something similar to this is reported from a group of the Tabiʿun.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated from al-Dahhak regarding the verse that he said: "It only refers to adultery and does not refer to marriage."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr something similar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from ʿIkrimah something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse that he said: "The adulterer from among the People of the Qiblah does not commit adultery except with a female adulterer like himself from among the People of the Qiblah, or a polytheist woman from outside the People of the Qiblah. And the female adulterer from among the People of the Qiblah does not commit adultery except with a male adulterer like herself from among the People of the Qiblah, or a polytheist man from outside the People of the Qiblah. And adultery is forbidden to the believers."

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: "There was a woman called Umm Mahzul, who used to fornicate and would stipulate that he spend on her. A man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to marry her, so Allah revealed: ﴿The adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist﴾."

Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "There was a man called Marthad, who used to carry captives from Makkah until he brought them to Madinah. In Makkah there was a prostitute called ʿAnaq, who was a friend of his." He mentioned a story in which: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I marry ʿAnaq?' He did not answer me at all until the verse was revealed: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾, the verse. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Marthad, ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾, so do not marry her.'"

Ibn Jarir narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr regarding the verse that he said: "They were known women. A man from among the poor Muslims would marry one of them so that she would spend on him, and Allah forbade them from that."

Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning open prostitutes who were in the Jahiliyyah, who were adulteresses and polytheists, so Allah forbade marrying them to the believers.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Shu'bah, the mawla of Ibn Abbas, who said: "I was with Ibn Abbas when a man came to him and said: 'I used to pursue a woman and I had from her what Allah had forbidden me. Allah has granted me repentance from her, and I wish to marry her.' The people said: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾. Ibn Abbas said: 'This is not the place of this verse. They were prostitutes who openly displayed themselves, who would place banners at their doors, by which people would recognize them. So Allah revealed this verse. Marry her, and if there is any sin in it, it is upon me.'"

Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn ʿAdi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The adulterer who has been flogged does not marry except one like himself."

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that a man married a woman, then he committed adultery and the prescribed punishment was carried out on him. They brought him to ʿAli, and he separated him from his wife and said: "Do not marry except a flogged woman like yourself."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 24, verse 1–3 (part 1 of 2):

Ibn Mardawayh reported from Ibn ʿAbbas and Ibn al-Zubayr that they both said: "Surat al-Nur was revealed at Madinah."

Al-Hakim, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in al-Shuʿab reported from ʿAʾishah, as a marfuʿ report: "Do not let them (women) live in upper rooms, and do not teach them writing; but teach them spinning and Surat al-Nur." (The phrase "i.e., the women" is in the text.)

Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi reported from Mujahid, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "Teach your men Surat al-Ma'idah, and teach your women Surat al-Nur." This is a mursal report.

Abu ʿUbayd in his Fada'il reported from Harithah ibn Mudarrib, who said: ʿUmar ibn al-Khattab wrote to us: "Learn Surat al-Nisa', al-Ahzab and al-Nur."

In the name of Allah, the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate.

﴿A surah which We have sent down and made obligatory, and in which We have sent down clear verses, that you may remember.﴾ ﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator: flog each one of them a hundred lashes. And let not pity for them take hold of you in the religion of Allah, if you believe in Allah and the Last Day. And let a group of the believers witness their punishment.﴾ ﴿The fornicator marries none but a fornicatress or an idolatress, and the fornicatress is married by none but a fornicator or an idolater; and that has been forbidden to the believers.﴾

(p-996) Al-surah linguistically means a noble rank, and for this reason a portion of the Qur'an is called a surah. From it is the saying of Zuhayr:

"Did you not see that Allah has given you a surah (rank), so that every king below it wavers?"

That is, a rank. The majority read surah with a nominative ending (surah-un), and there are two possibilities in this: first, that it is the predicate of an omitted subject, i.e., "this is a surah"; al-Zajjaj, al-Farra' and al-Mubarrad preferred this, saying: because it is indefinite, and one does not begin with an indefinite noun in every position.

The second possibility is that it is the subject, and beginning with an indefinite noun is permitted because it is qualified by His words "which We have sent down" (anzalnaha), and the predicate is "the fornicatress and the fornicator." The meaning would be: "the surah which is sent down and made obligatory is such-and-such," since a surah is an expression for a sequence of verses having a beginning and an end. This is a sound meaning, and there is no basis for what the earlier scholars said, that beginning with it is prohibited because it is indefinite; it is an indefinite noun specified by a qualifier, and beginning with it is agreed upon as permissible.

It has been said: it is a subject whose predicate is omitted, with the sense: "among what has been revealed to you is a surah." This was rejected, because the context calls for explaining the status of this noble surah, not for stating that among what was revealed to the Prophet (ﷺ) there is a surah of such-and-such a status.

Al-Hasan ibn ʿAbd al-ʿAziz, ʿIsa al-Thaqafi, ʿIsa al-Kufi, Mujahid, Abu Haywah and Talhah ibn Musarrif read it in the accusative (surata). There are several possibilities in this: the first is that it is accusative by a verb omitted and not explained by what follows, its estimate being "recite a surah" or "read a surah."

The second is that it is accusative by a hidden verb which is explained by what follows, according to what is said regarding the construction where the verb is occupied with its pronoun: i.e., "We sent down a surah, We have sent it down." Thus "anzalnaha" here has no place in grammatical analysis, because it is an explanatory clause; unlike the previous possibility, where it is in the accusative position as a qualifier of "surah."

The third possibility is that it is accusative as an exhortation, i.e., "take a surah" (duka surah). This was said by the author of al-Kashshaf. Abu Hayyan rejected it, saying that it is not permissible to omit the particle of exhortation.

The fourth is that it is accusative as a circumstantial (hal) from the pronoun of "anzalnaha." Al-Farra' said: it is a circumstantial from the ha' and alif, and a circumstantial from a pronoun may precede it. On this view the pronoun in "anzalnaha" does not refer to "surah" but to the rulings, as if it were said: "We sent down the rulings in the state of being a surah from the surahs of the Qur'an."

Ibn Kathir and Abu ʿAmr read "wa-farradnaha" with shaddah (intensive), and the rest read it without shaddah.

Abu ʿAmr said: "farradnaha" with shaddah means: We divided it in its sending down, portion by portion; and al-fard means cutting. It may also be that the shaddah indicates multiplicity or emphasis. The meaning of the lightened form is: We made it obligatory and made it something decided upon. It has also been said: We obligated you to act upon it; and it has been said: We determined the prescribed limits within it. Al-fard means determination, and from it is "Indeed He who has imposed upon you the Qur'an" (28:85). "And We sent down in it clear verses": that is, We sent down within its folds and contents. The meaning of their being clear is that their indication of what they signify is evident. The repetition of "anzalna" is for complete care in sending down this surah, because of the rulings it contains.

﴿The fornicatress and the fornicator﴾: this begins the detailed explanation of what was stated in summary among the clear verses. It is in the nominative as a subject, and the predicate is "flog each one of them"; or it is in the predicative sense for "surah," as has preceded. Zina is the intercourse of a man with a woman in her private part without marriage or the semblance of marriage.

It has also been said: it is the insertion of a private part into a private part which is naturally desired and legally forbidden. The fornicatress is the woman who submits to fornication and enables it, as the form indicates, not the one who is coerced; likewise the fornicator. The entry of the fa' into the predicate is because the subject implies the sense of a condition, according to the view of al-Akhfash. As for the view of Sibawayh, the predicate is omitted, and the estimate is: "In what is recited to you, the ruling on the fornicatress..." Then He explained that with His words: "flog."

Al-jald means striking; one says: "jaladahu" when he struck his skin, like "batanahu" when he struck his belly, and "ra'asahu" when he struck his head. His words "a hundred lashes" are the punishment for the free, adult, unmarried fornicator, and likewise the fornicatress. The Sunnah established an addition to this lashing, which is banishment for a year. As for the slave, male and female, each receives fifty lashes, based on His words: "If they commit a gross indecency, then upon them is half the punishment for free chaste women" (4:25). This is explicit regarding female slaves, and male slaves are added to them for lack of a distinguishing factor. As for the one who is muhsan (married), the penalty is stoning, by the authentic, widely transmitted Sunnah and by the consensus of the people of knowledge; indeed, and by the Qur'an whose wording was abrogated while its ruling remains, which is: "The elderly man and the elderly woman, if they commit fornication, stone them absolutely." A group of the people of knowledge added a hundred lashes along with stoning. We have clarified what is correct in this matter in our commentary on al-Muntaqa. Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 24, verse 1–3 (part 2 of 2):

Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn al-Mundhir and Ibn Abi Hatim narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding ﴿And let a group of the believers witness their punishment﴾ that he said: "The group (ṭāʾifah) is a man or more."

Abd al-Razzaq, al-Firyabi, Saʿid ibn Mansur, Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh (al-Nasikh wa'l-Mansukh, on abrogation), Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan, and al-Diya al-Maqdisi in al-Mukhtarah narrated through the route of Saʿid ibn Jubayr from Ibn Abbas regarding His saying: ﴿The adulterer does not marry﴾ that he said: "This is not about marriage (nikah) but about intercourse (jima'). No one commits adultery with her when he commits adultery except an adulterer or a polytheist." ﴿And that is forbidden to the believers﴾ meaning adultery.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Mujahid regarding His saying: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾ that he said: "The women in the Jahiliyyah were prostitutes (baghiyyat), and among them was a beautiful woman called Umm Jamil. A man from among the Muslims would marry one of them so that she would spend on him from her earnings. So Allah, glory be to Him, forbade any of the Muslims from marrying them." This is a mursal report.

Abd ibn Humayd narrated from Sulayman ibn Yasar something similar, in brief.

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from ʿAtaʾ from Ibn Abbas, who said: "In the Jahiliyyah there were prostitutes, the prostitutes of such-and-such a family and the prostitutes of such-and-such a family. So Allah said: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾, the verse... and Allah settled that matter concerning the affair of the Jahiliyyah." Something similar to this is reported from a group of the Tabiʿun.

Ibn Abi Shaybah and Abd ibn Humayd narrated from al-Dahhak regarding the verse that he said: "It only refers to adultery and does not refer to marriage."

Abd ibn Humayd and Ibn Jarir narrated from Saʿid ibn Jubayr something similar.

Ibn Abi Shaybah narrated from ʿIkrimah something similar. Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas regarding this verse that he said: "The adulterer from among the People of the Qiblah does not commit adultery except with a female adulterer like himself from among the People of the Qiblah, or a polytheist woman from outside the People of the Qiblah. And the female adulterer from among the People of the Qiblah does not commit adultery except with a male adulterer like herself from among the People of the Qiblah, or a polytheist man from outside the People of the Qiblah. And adultery is forbidden to the believers."

Ahmad, Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr, who said: "There was a woman called Umm Mahzul, who used to fornicate and would stipulate that he spend on her. A man from the Companions of the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) wished to marry her, so Allah revealed: ﴿The adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist﴾."

Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, al-Tirmidhi (who graded it hasan), al-Nasa'i, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, al-Hakim (who authenticated it), Ibn Mardawayh and al-Bayhaqi narrated from the hadith of Amr ibn Shu'ayb, from his father, from his grandfather, who said: "There was a man called Marthad, who used to carry captives from Makkah until he brought them to Madinah. In Makkah there was a prostitute called ʿAnaq, who was a friend of his." He mentioned a story in which: "I came to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and said: 'O Messenger of Allah, shall I marry ʿAnaq?' He did not answer me at all until the verse was revealed: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress﴾, the verse. So the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'O Marthad, ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist, and the adulteress is not married except by an adulterer or a polytheist, and that is forbidden to the believers﴾, so do not marry her.'"

Ibn Jarir narrated from Abd Allah ibn Amr regarding the verse that he said: "They were known women. A man from among the poor Muslims would marry one of them so that she would spend on him, and Allah forbade them from that."

Abu Dawud in his Nasikh, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi narrated from Ibn Abbas that it was revealed concerning open prostitutes who were in the Jahiliyyah, who were adulteresses and polytheists, so Allah forbade marrying them to the believers.

Ibn Abi Shaybah, Abd ibn Humayd, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh narrated through the route of Shu'bah, the mawla of Ibn Abbas, who said: "I was with Ibn Abbas when a man came to him and said: 'I used to pursue a woman and I had from her what Allah had forbidden me. Allah has granted me repentance from her, and I wish to marry her.' The people said: ﴿The adulterer does not marry except an adulteress or a polytheist﴾. Ibn Abbas said: 'This is not the place of this verse. They were prostitutes who openly displayed themselves, who would place banners at their doors, by which people would recognize them. So Allah revealed this verse. Marry her, and if there is any sin in it, it is upon me.'"

Abu Dawud, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn ʿAdi, Ibn Mardawayh and al-Hakim narrated from Abu Hurayrah, who said: The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: "The adulterer who has been flogged does not marry except one like himself."

Saʿid ibn Mansur and Ibn al-Mundhir narrated from ʿAli ibn Abi Talib that a man married a woman, then he committed adultery and the prescribed punishment was carried out on him. They brought him to ʿAli, and he separated him from his wife and said: "Do not marry except a flogged woman like yourself."

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 24, verse 4–10 (part 1 of 2):

His saying: ﴿And those who accuse⦅ ﴾ — he used "throwing" (al-ramy) metaphorically for insulting someone with the vile act of fornication, because it is an offence committed by speech, as al-Nabigha said:

"And the wound of the tongue is like the wound of the hand."

Another said:

"He hurled at me a matter from which I and my father were innocent, and for the sake of hunger he hurled it at me."

This insult with this particular vile act is called qadhf (false accusation of unchastity). By "the chaste women" (al-muhsanat) is meant women. They were singled out for mention because accusing them is more shameful and the disgrace in them is greater. Men are included with women in this ruling without any disagreement among the scholars of this community. We have compiled a treatise on this, in which we refuted some of the later scholars of the eleventh century who disputed it.

It has been said that the verse covers both men and women, and the implied phrase is "and the chaste persons" (wa-al-anfus al-muhsanat). This is supported by His saying, in another verse: ﴿and chaste women from among the women﴾, for specifying that they are "from among the women" indicates that the word "chaste" (al-muhsanat) includes other than women; otherwise the specification would have little meaning. It has also been said that by "al-muhsanat" He meant the private parts (furuj), as He said: ﴿and she who guarded her chastity (ahsanat farjaha)﴾ [al-Anbiya' 91], so the verse encompasses men and women.

It has been said that although the word "al-muhsanat" is for women, here it includes women and men by way of predominance (taghlib). But this is objectionable, since giving predominance to women over men is not known in the language of the Arabs. The meaning of "al-muhsanat" here is "the chaste" (al-afifa), and the term ihsan and its range of meanings has already been discussed in the surah of al-Nisa'.

The scholars have lengthy discussions regarding the conditions to be considered in the one accused and the accuser, which are fully developed in the books of jurisprudence (fiqh). Some of them are derived from evidence, and some are merely pure opinion.

The majority (al-Jumhur) read "wa-al-muhsanat" with a fatha on the ṣad. Yahya ibn Wathhab read it with a kasra.

The majority of scholars hold that there is no hadd (prescribed punishment) upon one who accuses a disbeliever, male or female.

Al-Zuhri, Sa'id ibn al-Musayyib and Ibn Abi Layla said that the hadd is obligatory upon him.

The majority also hold that a slave is flogged forty lashes.

Ibn Mas'ud, Umar ibn Abd al-Aziz and Qabisa said: he is flogged eighty.

Al-Qurtubi said: The scholars agree that a free person is not flogged for a slave if he slanders him, because their ranks differ. It is established in the Sahih from him (ﷺ) that whoever accuses his slave of fornication, the prescribed punishment will be enforced upon him on the Day of Resurrection, unless it is as he said.

Then He, glorified is He, stated a condition for enforcing the hadd upon one who accuses chaste women, saying: ﴿then they do not bring four witnesses﴾, meaning, who testify to the occurrence of fornication by them. The word "then" (thumma) indicates that the testimony of the witnesses may be given outside the session of the accusation, and this is the view of the majority, though Malik disagreed on this point.

The apparent meaning of the verse is that the witnesses may be gathered together or separately; al-Hasan and Malik disagreed with this. If the witnesses do not complete four, they become slanderers and are punished with the hadd of qadhf.

Al-Hasan and al-Sha'bi said: there is no hadd upon the witnesses nor upon the one they testified against. This is also the view of Ahmad, Abu Hanifa and Muhammad ibn al-Hasan.

This is refuted by what occurred in the caliphate of Umar (may Allah be pleased with him), when he flogged the three who testified against al-Mughira for fornication, and none of the Companions (may Allah be pleased with them all) disagreed.

The majority read ﴿four witnesses﴾ with the idafa of "four" to "witnesses." Abdullah ibn Muslim ibn Yasar and Abu Zur'a ibn Amr read "arba'a" with tanwin.

The grammatical status of "shuhada'" in this reading has been disputed. It has been said it is a tamyiz (specification). This is rejected on the grounds that the specified noun for numbers from three to ten is put in the genitive (idafa), as is established in the science of grammar. It has also been said that it is in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier (hal). This is rejected on the grounds that the hal does not come from an indefinite noun that has not been specified.

It has been said that "shuhada'" is in the genitive position as an attribute (na't) of "arba'a," and since it contains the feminine ending (alif al-ta'nith), it is not declined. Al-Nahhas said: it is permissible that "shuhada'" be in the accusative position as an object, meaning: "then they do not produce four witnesses." Ibn Jinni strengthened this reading, but Sibawayh's statement refutes it, that the tanwin of the number and leaving off its idafa is permissible only in poetry.

(p-999) Then He explained what is obligatory upon the accuser, saying: ﴿flog them eighty lashes﴾. Jald is striking, as has been mentioned. Mujalada is striking on or with hides, and then it was used metaphorically for striking with a stick, a sword and other things. From this is the saying of Qays ibn al-Khatim:

"I strike them on the day of al-Hadiqa, bare-headed, as if my hand with the sword were a juggler's whip."

The explanation of jald has already been given shortly. The accusative of "eighty" is like the accusative of the verbal nouns (masadir), and "lashes" (jaldatan) is accusative as a specification (tamyiz). The clause ﴿and do not accept their testimony ever⦅ ﴾ is joined to "flog" (ijlidu), meaning: combine for them the two matters: the flogging and the refusal to accept their testimony, because by slander they have become no longer upright (ʿudul) but rather corrupt (fasiqun), as Allah has judged in the end of this verse. The lam in "for them" is related to a deleted element which is a circumstantial qualifier (hal) of "testimony"; had it been placed after it, it would have been an attribute of it. The meaning of "ever" (abadan) is: as long as they are alive.

Then He, glorified is He, explained their ruling after the slander had come from them, their persistence in it, and their not returning to repentance, saying: ﴿And those are the corrupt (al-fasiqun)﴾. This is a resumptive clause confirming what precedes it. Fisq is departing from obedience and exceeding the limit by disobedience. Abu al-Baqa' permitted that this clause be in the accusative position as a circumstantial qualifier.

Then He, glorified is He, explained that this perpetual refusal of their testimony applies together with the absence of repentance, saying: ﴿except those who repent﴾ [al-Ma'idah 33–34]. This clause is in the accusative position as an exception, since it follows a positive statement. It has also been said it may be in the genitive position as a substitute (badal). The meaning of repentance has already been established. The meaning of ﴿after that﴾ is after their committing the sin of slander. The meaning of "and reform" is reforming their deeds, of which the sin of slander is part, and compensating for it through repentance and submission to the hadd.

The people of knowledge have differed over whether this exception refers to the two preceding clauses: the clause on non-acceptance of testimony and the clause on judging them corrupt, or to the last clause. This disagreement comes after their agreement that it does not refer to the clause of flogging, but the repentant is flogged just like the persistent; and after their agreement too that this exception refers to the clause of judging them corrupt, so the point of disagreement is whether it refers to the clause of non-acceptance of testimony or not. The majority said: this exception refers to both clauses. So when the slanderer repents, his testimony is accepted and corruption is removed from him, because the cause of rejecting it was what he was characterized by of corruption due to the slander; when that is removed by repentance, by consensus, the testimony is accepted.

Al-Qadi Shurayh, Ibrahim al-Nakha'i, al-Hasan al-Basri, Sa'id ibn Jubayr, Makhul, Abd al-Rahman ibn Zayd, Sufyan al-Thawri and Abu Hanifa said: this exception refers to the clause judging them corrupt, not to the clause of non-acceptance of testimony. So by repentance the slanderer's attribute of corruption is removed, but his testimony is never accepted.

Al-Sha'bi and al-Dahhak went to a distinction, saying: his testimony is not accepted even if he repents, unless he confesses on himself that he uttered the slander; then his testimony is accepted.

The view of the majority is the correct one, because restricting the qualifier to the last clause alone, when the speech is one in a single legal matter from one speaker, contradicts what the language of the Arabs requires. The priority of the last clause, connected to the qualifier, is that the qualifier is for what precedes it, the only point being that restricting the last clause by the connected qualifier is more apparent than restricting what precedes it by it, and for this reason it was agreed upon; and that it is more apparent does not negate that it applies to what precedes it in its apparent sense.

The usuli scholars have extended discussion on a qualifier that comes after a series of clauses, in what is known to those who know that discipline, and the truth is this. Arguing from what occurs at times of qualifiers returning to all the preceding clauses, and at times to some of them, is not a valid proof and is not suitable for deduction, for that may be due to evidence, as occurs here with the consensus that this exception does not return to the clause of flogging.

What supports and strengthens what we have established is that the barrier to accepting testimony, which is the corruption caused by slander, has been removed, so nothing remains that requires rejecting the testimony.

The scholars differed over the manner of the slanderer's repentance. Umar ibn al-Khattab, al-Sha'bi, al-Dahhak and the people of Madina said: his repentance is only by his denying that slander which occurred from him and for which the hadd was enforced upon him.

A group, including Malik and others, said: his repentance is by his improving his condition, correcting his conduct, regretting what he committed, asking Allah's forgiveness for it, and resolving not to return to its like, even if he does not retract his statement nor take back his words.

This is supported by the verses and the hadiths concerning repentance, for they are absolute and not restricted by such a condition.

The Ummah has agreed that repentance erases the sin, even if it is disbelief; so it erases what is less than disbelief all the more. Thus al-Qurtubi reported the consensus.

Abu Ubayd said: the exception refers to the preceding clauses. The one who accuses another of fornication is not greater in crime than the one who commits fornication, and the fornicator, if he repents, his testimony is accepted, because the one who repents from sin is like one who has no sin; and if Allah accepts the repentance of the servant, then the servants accepting it is more fitting. Moreover, this kind of exception is found in several places in the Qur'an, among them His saying: ﴿Indeed, the penalty of those who wage war against Allah﴾ up to His saying: ﴿except those who repent﴾, and there is no doubt that this exception refers to the whole.

Al-Zajjaj said: the accuser is not greater in crime than the disbeliever, so his right, if he repents and reforms, is that his testimony be accepted. He said: His saying "ever" means as long as he is an accuser, just as one says the testimony of a disbeliever is never accepted, meaning as long as he is a disbeliever. Finished.

The clause ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾ is a justification for what the exception contains of non-punishment of the accuser after repentance, and his becoming forgiven and shown mercy by the Most Merciful, the Most Compassionate, not corrupt, nor having his testimony rejected, nor his uprightness (adala) removed.

Then, after mentioning the ruling on slander in general, He, glorified is He, mentioned the ruling on a type of slander, which is the husband accusing the wife who is under his marriage contract, saying: ﴿And those who accuse their wives and have no witnesses except themselves﴾, meaning: they have no witnesses who testify to the fornication with which they accused them, except themselves, in the nominative as a substitute (badal) for "witnesses." It has been said that the accusative is also permissible as the predicate of "yakun" (there is not). Al-Zajjaj said: or in the accusative as an exception, in the less preferred manner.

﴿Then the testimony of one of them is four testimonies﴾. The Kufans read "arba'un" with the nominative, taking it as the predicate of ﴿the testimony of one of them﴾, meaning: the testimony of one of them which removes from him the hadd of slander is four testimonies.

(p-1000) The people of Madina and Abu 'Amr read "arba'a" with the accusative as an absolute object (masdar), and ﴿the testimony of one of them﴾ is then the predicate of a deleted subject, meaning: so what is obligatory is the testimony of one of them; or it is a subject whose predicate is deleted, meaning: so the testimony of one of them is obligatory.

It has also been said that "arba'a" is accusative by the implied phrase: so it is incumbent upon them that one of them testify four testimonies. The phrase "by Allah" is connected to "testimony" or to "testimonies," and the clause ﴿that he is indeed among the truthful﴾ is what is testified to. Its original form was that the preposition was dropped and the particle "inna" was given a kasra, and the governing element was suspended from it.

Commentary of al-Shawkani (Fath al-Qadir) on surah 24, verses 4–10 (part 2 of 2):

The fifth [testimony]: The Seven [readers] and others read al-Khamisah ("the fifth") in the nominative (bi'l-raf'), as a subject (ibtida'), and its predicate is ﴿that the curse of Allah be upon him if he is of the liars﴾. Abu 'Abd al-Rahman, Talhah and 'Asim (in the transmission of Hafs) read al-Khamisata ("the fifth") in the accusative (bi'l-nasb), on the sense of "and let him testify the fifth testimony." The meaning of ﴿if he is of the liars﴾ is: in what he accused her of, namely adultery.

The majority read ﴿anna﴾ ("that") with the doubled nun, in ﴿that the curse of Allah﴾. Nafi' read it with the single nun (takhfif). According to Nafi's reading, the subject of anna is the pronoun of the matter (damir al-sha'n), la'nat Allah is the subject of a nominal clause, 'alayhi is its predicate, and the whole clause is the predicate of anna. According to the reading of the majority, la'nat Allah is the noun of anna. Sibawayh said: "Anna is not lightened in speech when nouns follow it unless you intend the heavy form." Al-Akhfash said: "I know of no form better in Arabic than the heavy (thaqilah)."

﴿And it averts from her the punishment﴾: that is, from the woman. The intended punishment is the worldly one, which is the hadd (prescribed penalty). The agent of yadra'u ("averts") is His saying ﴿that she testify four testimonies by Allah﴾. The meaning is that her testimony of four testimonies by Allah averts from the woman the hadd, [namely] that he is ﴿of the liars﴾, and the fifth ﴿[testimony]﴾ in the accusative as a conjunction with "four," i.e., "and let her testify the fifth likewise." This was read by Hafs, al-Hasan, al-Sulami, Talhah and al-A'mash. The rest read it in the nominative as a subject, and its predicate is ﴿that the wrath of Allah be upon her if he is of the truthful﴾ regarding what he accused her of, namely adultery. Restricting the wrath to the woman is for emphasis against her, because she is the root and origin of immorality; and because women commonly use cursing a great deal, and despite their frequent use of it, it does not carry great weight in their hearts, unlike wrath.

﴿And were it not for the bounty of Allah upon you and His mercy﴾: the answer to lawla ("were it not") is omitted. Al-Zajjaj said: the meaning is "And were it not for the bounty of Allah, the liar among them would have incurred a great punishment."

Then He, glory be to Him, clarified His abundant forgiveness toward those who repent and His immense, far-reaching wisdom, saying: ﴿and that Allah is Oft-Returning, All-Wise﴾: that is, He turns back (to mercy) toward whoever repents to Him and returns from his disobedience through repentance, granting him forgiveness; All-Wise in what He legislated for His servants of li'an and imposed upon them of the prescribed penalties.

Abu Dawud in his Nasikh and Ibn al-Mundhir related from Ibn 'Abbas, regarding His saying ﴿except those who repent﴾, that he said: "Allah relents toward them from wickedness, but as for testimony, it is not permitted."

Sa'id ibn Mansur and Ibn Jarir related from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab that he said to Abu Bakrah: "If you repent, I will accept your testimony."

Ibn Mardawayh related from him (Ibn 'Abbas) that he said: "Their repentance is their denial of themselves; if they deny themselves, their testimony is accepted."

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir and al-Bayhaqi in his Sunan related from Ibn 'Abbas that he said: "Whoever repents and makes amends, his testimony is accepted in the Book of Allah." There are narrations from the Followers (tabi'un) on this point.

The story of al-Mughirah's slander in the caliphate of 'Umar is transmitted through well-known chains.

al-Bukhari, al-Tirmidhi and Ibn Majah related from Ibn 'Abbas: "That Hilal ibn Umayyah slandered his wife before the Prophet (ﷺ) with Sharik ibn Sahma'. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'The evidence, or else a hadd on your back.' He said: 'O Messenger of Allah, when one of us sees a man on his wife, he goes out seeking evidence?' The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) kept saying: 'The evidence, or else a hadd on your back.' Hilal said: 'By Him who sent you with the truth, I am truthful, and Allah will surely send down what will clear my back from the hadd.' Jibril descended and brought down upon him ﴿And those who accuse their wives﴾ until ﴿if he is of the truthful﴾. The Prophet (ﷺ) turned away and sent for them both. Hilal came and testified, while the Prophet (ﷺ) was saying: 'Allah knows that one of you two is a liar; will any of you repent?' Then she stood and testified. When she reached the fifth, they halted her and said: 'It is binding.' She hesitated and drew back, until we thought she would retract. Then she said: 'I will not disgrace my people for the rest of the day,' and she went on. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Watch her; if she brings forth a child with dark eyes, large buttocks and thick calves, then it belongs to Sharik ibn Sahma'.' She brought forth one such. The Prophet (ﷺ) said: 'Were it not for what has passed of the Book of Allah, there would have been a matter between me and her.'"

Abu Dawud al-Tayalisi, 'Abd al-Razzaq, Ahmad, 'Abd ibn Humayd, Abu Dawud, Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, Ibn Abi Hatim and Ibn Mardawayh related this story from Ibn 'Abbas in a lengthy form.

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others related it, but they did not name the man or the woman.

At the end of the story, the Prophet (ﷺ) said to him: "Go, you have no claim over her." He said: "O Messenger of Allah, what about my property?" He said: "You have no property. If you spoke truthfully about her, then it is for what you made lawful of her private part; and if you lied about her, then that is further away from you than her."

al-Bukhari, Muslim and others related from Sahl ibn Sa'd that he said: "'Uwaymir came to 'Asim ibn 'Adi and said: 'Ask the Messenger of Allah: Tell me, a man found another man with his wife and killed him; is he to be killed for it, or what should he do?' 'Asim asked the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ), and the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) disliked the questions. 'Uwaymir said: 'By Allah, I will surely go to the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) and ask him.' He came to him and found that it had already been revealed to him. He summoned the two of them and had them perform li'an between them. 'Uwaymir said: 'If I take her away, O Messenger of Allah, I will have lied about her.' He divorced her before the Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) commanded him, and it became a sunnah for those who perform li'an. The Messenger of Allah (ﷺ) said: 'Watch her; if she brings forth a child that is black, with intense black eyes and large buttocks, then I do not think he is other than truthful; and if she brings forth one that is reddish, like a lizard, then I do not think he is other than a liar.' She brought forth one like the disliked description." There are many hadiths on this subject, and what we have mentioned suffices.

'Abd al-Razzaq related from 'Umar ibn al-Khattab, 'Ali and Ibn Mas'ud that they said: "The two who perform li'an never come together again, ever."
