"Innama" is one of the particles of restriction (sigha al-hasr). The meaning is: faith is not complete and does not perfect until one is [sincere] toward Allah and His Messenger.

The clause "﴿And when they are with him on a gathering matter﴾" is conjoined to "they believed" and lies within the scope of the relative clause (silah) with it. That is: when they are with the Messenger of Allah on a gathering matter, meaning a matter of obedience around which they gather, such as the Friday prayer (jumu'ah), the sacrifice (nahr), the festival of breaking the fast (fitr), jihad, and the like. The matter is called "gathering" (jami') as an intensification.

﴿They do not leave until they seek his permission.﴾ The exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit on Friday and a man wished to leave the mosque for a need or an excuse, he would not leave until he stood facing the Prophet ﷺ where he could see him. He would thereby make known that he had stood up to ask permission, and [the Prophet] would grant permission to whoever he wished of them. Mujahid said: The permission of the imam on Friday is that he gestures with his hand.

Al-Zajjaj said: Allah informed that when the believers are with His Prophet in a matter in which the community is needed, they do not leave until they seek his permission. Likewise, it is fitting that they be with the imam, not opposing him, nor turning back from him in any of their gatherings except with his permission. The imam may grant permission, and he may refuse, according to what he sees, based on the saying of the Most High: ﴿So permit whom you will of them﴾. Al-Yamani recited "upon a matter that is collective" (ʿalā amrin jamīʿin).

The conclusion: the "gathering matter" (al-amr al-jami') or "the collective" (al-jami') is that whose benefit or harm is general, the grave matter that requires the gathering of people of opinion and experience.

The scholars said: Every matter upon which the Muslims gather with the imam, they do not oppose him in it, nor turn back from it except with permission. Then the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. Thus He made clear that those who seek permission are the believers in Allah and His Messenger, just as He had first ruled that the believers of complete faith are those who combine belief in both of them with seeking permission.

﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs﴾, meaning: when the believers seek the permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for some of the matters that concern them, he grants permission to whomever he wishes of them, and withholds it from whomever he wishes, according to what the benefit that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sees requires. Then Allah the Exalted directed him to seek forgiveness for them. This indicates that if the seeking of permission is for a valid excuse, it is not free of some trace of worldly affairs taking precedence over the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: abundantly forgiving and merciful, reaching in both to the limit beyond which there is no limit.

﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾. This sentence is resumed, confirming what precedes it, meaning: do not make his calling you like the calling of one of you to another in being lax, in some circumstances, about responding, or returning without permission, or raising the voice. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: The meaning is, say: "O Messenger of Allah" gently and softly, and do not say: "O Muhammad" in a harsh manner. Qatada said: He commanded them to honor him and to magnify him. It was also said: The meaning is: do not expose yourselves to the supplication of the Messenger against you by angering him, for his supplication is binding.

﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, hiding behind one another.﴾ Al-Tasallul: going out secretly. It is said: "So-and-so slipped away from among his companions" when he left from among them. Al-Liwadh is from al-mulawadhah, which is to conceal oneself behind something for fear of being seen. Its origin is that one seeks shelter with that and that with this. Al-lawdh is what surrounds a mountain. It was also said: al-liwadh is deviating from one thing to another in secrecy.

The accusative of "liwadhan" is circumstantial (hal), meaning: hiding behind one another, one taking refuge with another and joining himself to him. It was also said: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar) for a hidden verb, which is in reality the circumstance, meaning: they hide behind one another.

Zayd ibn Qutayb read "lawadhan" with a fatha on the lam.

In the verse is an explanation of what the hypocrites used to do. They would slip away from the Friday prayer, hiding behind one another, joining one to another in concealment from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Friday was the heaviest day upon the hypocrites, because of what they saw of the gathering for prayer and the sermon, so they would flee from attendance, slip away secretly, and some would conceal themselves behind others and join with them.

It was also said: al-liwadh is fleeing from jihad, and al-Hasan said so. From this is the saying of Hassan:

"And Quraysh roams around from you, hiding behind one another, not preserving [the bond], and their intellects have dried up."

﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾. The fa' is for the ordering of what follows upon what precedes, meaning: those who oppose the command of the Prophet ﷺ by abandoning acting upon its requirement. The verb "opposing" is transitive with "an" (from) though it is transitive by itself, because it is made to imply the sense of turning away or averting. It was also said: the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted, because He is the true Commander. And ﴿lest a trial befall them﴾ is the object of "let beware," and its subject is the relative pronoun.

The meaning: so let those who oppose the command of Allah, or the command of His Messenger, or the command of both of them, beware of a trial befalling them. ﴿Or a painful punishment strike them﴾, meaning in the Hereafter, just as the trial from which He warned them of its befalling them is in this world. The particle "or" (aw) is for preventing a [third] alternative.

Al-Qurtubi said: The jurists have argued from this verse that the command is for obligation. The reasoning is that Allah the Exalted warned against opposing His command and threatened punishment for it by His saying: ﴿lest a trial befall them﴾ and so on. Therefore, complying with His command is obligatory and opposing it is forbidden. The "trial" here is not restricted to a particular kind of trial. It was said: [it is] killing. It was said: [it is] the sealing of their hearts.

(p. 1031) Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: "ʿan" in this place is superfluous. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: it is not superfluous, but it has the meaning of "after," as in His saying: ﴿So he disobeyed the command of his Lord﴾, meaning: after the command of his Lord. The preferable view is what we have mentioned, namely the implication of meaning (tadmin).

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ of creatures in their entirety; so they are His possession. ﴿He already knows your condition, [O servants]﴾, meaning the states in which you are, so He will recompense you according to them. "Yaʿlamu" here means "ʿalima." ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him﴾ is conjoined to "your condition," meaning: He knows your condition and He knows the Day they are returned to Him, and He will recompense you for what you did on that Day. The linking of His knowledge with "the Day they are returned" rather than with the returning itself is for the increase of affirming His knowledge, since knowledge of the time of an event's occurrence entails knowledge of its occurrence in the most emphatic manner. ﴿Then He will inform them of what they did﴾, meaning He will tell them of the deeds they did, of which opposing the command is part. The apparent context indicates that this threat is for the hypocrites. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, nothing of their deeds being hidden from Him.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il reported from Urwa and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who both said: When Quraysh came in the year of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), they camped at Majma' al-Asyal from Rawmat Bi'r in Medina, their leader being Abu Sufyan. Ghatafan came and camped at Naqma beside Uhud. The news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he dug the trench (khandaq) around Medina, and the Muslims worked on it. Some men among the hypocrites lagged behind and began to make excuses for weak work, and they would slip away to their families without the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and without permission. When a Muslim faced a pressing need that could not be avoided, he would mention that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask his permission to go for his need, and he would grant it. When he had fulfilled his need, he returned. So Allah revealed concerning those: ﴿Indeed, the believers are those who have believed in Allah﴾ and the rest of the verse.

ʿAbd ibn Humayd and Ibn Abi Hatim reported from Sa'id ibn Jubayr concerning the verse that he said: It concerns jihad, the Friday prayer, and the two festivals.

Ibn Jarir, Ibn al-Mundhir, and Ibn Abi Hatim reported concerning His saying ﴿upon a gathering matter﴾ that he said: [It is] of the obedience of Allah, general.

Ibn Abi Hatim, Ibn Mardawayh, and Abu Na'im in al-Dala'il reported from him concerning His saying ﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger﴾ and the verse, that he said: It means like the calling of one of you when he calls his brother by name. Rather, honor him and say to him: "O Messenger of Allah, O Prophet of Allah."

Abd al-Ghani ibn Sa'id reported in his tafsir, and Abu Na'im in al-Dala'il, also from him concerning the verse, that he said: Do not shout at him from afar, "O Abu al-Qasim," but rather as Allah said in al-Hujurat: ﴿Indeed, those who lower their voices in the presence of the Messenger of Allah﴾.

Abu Dawud in his al-Marasil reported from Muqatil, who said: No one would leave because of a nosebleed or a breach of wind until he sought the permission of the Prophet ﷺ, indicating to him with the finger next to the thumb, and the Prophet ﷺ would grant him permission by a gesture of his hand. Among the hypocrites were some for whom the sermon and sitting in the mosque were burdensome. So whenever a man among the Muslims sought permission, the hypocrite would stand beside him, concealing himself behind him until he left. So Allah revealed ﴿Those who slip away among you, hiding behind one another﴾ and the verse.

Abu Ubayd in his Fada'il and al-Tabarani reported, al-Suyuti said with a good chain, from Uqba ibn Amir who said: I saw the Messenger of Allah ﷺ reading this verse at the end of Surat al-Nur, while placing his two fingers beneath his eyes, saying: ﴿with every thing, Seeing﴾.

The sentence "Believers are only..." (innama al-mu'minun) is a resumed clause (mustanafa), brought in to specify what preceded it of the rulings. "Innama" is one of the particles of restriction (sigha al-hasr). The meaning is: faith is not complete and does not perfect until one is [sincere] toward Allah and His Messenger.

The clause "﴿And when they are with him on a gathering matter﴾" is conjoined to "they believed" and lies within the scope of the relative clause (silah) with it. That is: when they are with the Messenger of Allah on a gathering matter, meaning a matter of obedience around which they gather, such as the Friday prayer (jumu'ah), the sacrifice (nahr), the festival of breaking the fast (fitr), jihad, and the like. The matter is called "gathering" (jami') as an intensification.

﴿They do not leave until they seek his permission.﴾ The exegetes said: When the Messenger of Allah ﷺ ascended the pulpit on Friday and a man wished to leave the mosque for a need or an excuse, he would not leave until he stood facing the Prophet ﷺ where he could see him. He would thereby make known that he had stood up to ask permission, and [the Prophet] would grant permission to whoever he wished of them. Mujahid said: The permission of the imam on Friday is that he gestures with his hand.

Al-Zajjaj said: Allah informed that when the believers are with His Prophet in a matter in which the community is needed, they do not leave until they seek his permission. Likewise, it is fitting that they be with the imam, not opposing him, nor turning back from him in any of their gatherings except with his permission. The imam may grant permission, and he may refuse, according to what he sees, based on the saying of the Most High: ﴿So permit whom you will of them﴾. Al-Yamani recited "upon a matter that is collective" (ʿalā amrin jamīʿin).

The conclusion: the "gathering matter" (al-amr al-jami') or "the collective" (al-jami') is that whose benefit or harm is general, the grave matter that requires the gathering of people of opinion and experience.

The scholars said: Every matter upon which the Muslims gather with the imam, they do not oppose him in it, nor turn back from it except with permission. Then the Exalted said: ﴿Indeed, those who ask your permission are those who believe in Allah and His Messenger﴾. Thus He made clear that those who seek permission are the believers in Allah and His Messenger, just as He had first ruled that the believers of complete faith are those who combine belief in both of them with seeking permission.

﴿So when they ask your permission for some of their affairs﴾, meaning: when the believers seek the permission of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ for some of the matters that concern them, he grants permission to whomever he wishes of them, and withholds it from whomever he wishes, according to what the benefit that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ sees requires. Then Allah the Exalted directed him to seek forgiveness for them. This indicates that if the seeking of permission is for a valid excuse, it is not free of some trace of worldly affairs taking precedence over the Hereafter. ﴿Indeed, Allah is Forgiving and Merciful﴾, meaning: abundantly forgiving and merciful, reaching in both to the limit beyond which there is no limit.

﴿Do not make the call of the Messenger among yourselves like the call of some of you to others﴾. This sentence is resumed, confirming what precedes it, meaning: do not make his calling you like the calling of one of you to another in being lax, in some circumstances, about responding, or returning without permission, or raising the voice. Sa'id ibn Jubayr and Mujahid said: The meaning is, say: "O Messenger of Allah" gently and softly, and do not say: "O Muhammad" in a harsh manner. Qatada said: He commanded them to honor him and to magnify him. It was also said: The meaning is: do not expose yourselves to the supplication of the Messenger against you by angering him, for his supplication is binding.

﴿Allah already knows those among you who slip away, hiding behind one another.﴾ Al-Tasallul: going out secretly. It is said: "So-and-so slipped away from among his companions" when he left from among them. Al-Liwadh is from al-mulawadhah, which is to conceal oneself behind something for fear of being seen. Its origin is that one seeks shelter with that and that with this. Al-lawdh is what surrounds a mountain. It was also said: al-liwadh is deviating from one thing to another in secrecy.

The accusative of "liwadhan" is circumstantial (hal), meaning: hiding behind one another, one taking refuge with another and joining himself to him. It was also said: it is in the accusative as a verbal noun (masdar) for a hidden verb, which is in reality the circumstance, meaning: they hide behind one another.

Zayd ibn Qutayb read "lawadhan" with a fatha on the lam.

In the verse is an explanation of what the hypocrites used to do. They would slip away from the Friday prayer, hiding behind one another, joining one to another in concealment from the Messenger of Allah ﷺ. Friday was the heaviest day upon the hypocrites, because of what they saw of the gathering for prayer and the sermon, so they would flee from attendance, slip away secretly, and some would conceal themselves behind others and join with them.

It was also said: al-liwadh is fleeing from jihad, and al-Hasan said so. From this is the saying of Hassan:

"And Quraysh roams around from you, hiding behind one another, not preserving [the bond], and their intellects have dried up."

﴿So let those who oppose his command beware﴾. The fa' is for the ordering of what follows upon what precedes, meaning: those who oppose the command of the Prophet ﷺ by abandoning acting upon its requirement. The verb "opposing" is transitive with "an" (from) though it is transitive by itself, because it is made to imply the sense of turning away or averting. It was also said: the pronoun refers to Allah the Exalted, because He is the true Commander. And ﴿lest a trial befall them﴾ is the object of "let beware," and its subject is the relative pronoun.

The meaning: so let those who oppose the command of Allah, or the command of His Messenger, or the command of both of them, beware of a trial befalling them. ﴿Or a painful punishment strike them﴾, meaning in the Hereafter, just as the trial from which He warned them of its befalling them is in this world. The particle "or" (aw) is for preventing a [third] alternative.

Al-Qurtubi said: The jurists have argued from this verse that the command is for obligation. The reasoning is that Allah the Exalted warned against opposing His command and threatened punishment for it by His saying: ﴿lest a trial befall them﴾ and so on. Therefore, complying with His command is obligatory and opposing it is forbidden. The "trial" here is not restricted to a particular kind of trial. It was said: [it is] killing. It was said: [it is] the sealing of their hearts.

(p. 1031) Abu Ubayda and al-Akhfash said: "ʿan" in this place is superfluous. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh said: it is not superfluous, but it has the meaning of "after," as in His saying: ﴿So he disobeyed the command of his Lord﴾, meaning: after the command of his Lord. The preferable view is what we have mentioned, namely the implication of meaning (tadmin).

﴿Unquestionably, to Allah belongs whatever is in the heavens and whatever is on the earth﴾ of creatures in their entirety; so they are His possession. ﴿He already knows your condition, [O servants]﴾, meaning the states in which you are, so He will recompense you according to them. "Yaʿlamu" here means "ʿalima." ﴿And the Day they are returned to Him﴾ is conjoined to "your condition," meaning: He knows your condition and He knows the Day they are returned to Him, and He will recompense you for what you did on that Day. The linking of His knowledge with "the Day they are returned" rather than with the returning itself is for the increase of affirming His knowledge, since knowledge of the time of an event's occurrence entails knowledge of its occurrence in the most emphatic manner. ﴿Then He will inform them of what they did﴾, meaning He will tell them of the deeds they did, of which opposing the command is part. The apparent context indicates that this threat is for the hypocrites. ﴿And Allah is Knowing of all things﴾, nothing of their deeds being hidden from Him.

Ibn Ishaq, Ibn al-Mundhir, and al-Bayhaqi in al-Dala'il reported from Urwa and Muhammad ibn Ka'b al-Qurazi, who both said: When Quraysh came in the year of the Confederates (al-Ahzab), they camped at Majma' al-Asyal from Rawmat Bi'r in Medina, their leader being Abu Sufyan. Ghatafan came and camped at Naqma beside Uhud. The news reached the Messenger of Allah ﷺ, so he dug the trench (khandaq) around Medina, and the Muslims worked on it. Some men among the hypocrites lagged behind and began to make excuses for weak work, and they would slip away to their families without the knowledge of the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and without permission. When a Muslim faced a pressing need that could not be avoided, he would mention that to the Messenger of Allah ﷺ and ask his permission to go for his need, and he would grant it. When he had fulfilled his need, he returned. So Allah revealed concerning those: ﴿Indeed, the believers are those who have believed in Allah﴾ and the rest of the verse.
